title: TrkB loss represses Vgf-centered MAPK output in Pvalb and thalamic glutamatergic neurons
exact_observed_result: Ntrk2 was reduced in 22/22 assayed Ntrk2 cell types and reached FDR in Pvalb GABA, thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic cells, and 155 MB Glut. The decisive non-target rows were Akap5 down in Pvalb GABA and Atp2a2 plus Vgf down in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; Ntrk1 and Ntrk3 did not reproduce those same-cell marker rows.
biological_interpretation: The CRISPRi response is a narrow TrkB-loss RNA state, not a pan-neurotrophin receptor state. Vgf is the most recurrent BDNF/TrkB-compatible output, while Akap5 and Atp2a2 mark distinct Pvalb and thalamic branches.

support.description: Ntrk2 loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut decreased the target and the Vgf/Atp2a2 branch.
Pvalb Ntrk2 decreased Akap5 while Ntrk3 drove an Arhgap12-only response; Ntrk3 and Ntrk1 did not move the Ntrk2/Braf thalamic Vgf/Atp2a2 module.

caveats: The broader Vgf recurrence after Ntrk2 perturbation is mostly nominal; only the 151 TH row passed 5% FDR.
The Nf1 and Pten opposition is based on weak whole-signature anticorrelations, not a direct FDR marker-gene reversal.
Ntrk1 and Ngfr target engagement was weak, so their null signatures are assay-limited comparators.

prior_expectation.summary: NTRK2/TrkB is a BDNF/NTF receptor feeding RAS-MAPK and PI3K cascades; Vgf is an established neurotrophin-inducible BDNF output, and adult TrkB signaling is known to matter in PV interneurons.

citations.citation: Bozdagi et al., Journal of Neuroscience, 2008.
Guyon et al., Journal of Neuroscience, 2021.
